title: Repeat visits to the same desk, two records compared
question: Do the City’s review metrics show the same number of repeat review visits as the routing table the permit-process screens used?
finding: For full-review alterations and new buildings filed 2015 to 2026, the review-metrics table shows Building plan check: 2.38 visits per permit (57% seen more than once) against 2.44 in the routing table; Planning zoning check: 1.86 visits per permit (50% seen more than once) against 1.9 in the routing table; Mechanical plan check: 1.73 visits per permit (39% seen more than once) against 1.78 in the routing table; Public Works street-use and mapping: 2.12 visits per permit (53% seen more than once) against 2.17 in the routing table.
how: Review rows (first reviews and rechecks) per permit and station, for permit types 1, 2 and 3; set beside the "where-the-time-goes" screen in the site’s “How the permit process works” page, which counted routing steps in the addenda routing table for the same kinds of permit filed since 2015.
limits: The two records count different things: the routing table logs every hand-off, including holds and processing desks, while the metrics table logs reviews only. A difference is not an error in either.

sources.t: DataSF: Building Permit Application Review Metrics (Building Inspection; table as of 17 Nov 2026)
Building Inspection via DataSF (data.sf.gov): Building Permits (DataSF)
